createScheduleApi.returns: ScheduleApi {schedule,levelAt,describe,levelInfo} (the schedule bound, so the clock reading is the only argument)

levelAt.returns: number (level from 1; a method of ScheduleApi; same as levelFor on the bound schedule)

describe.returns: LevelDescription {level,label,values,extended,final,next:LevelInfo|null,msUntilNext:number|null} (a method of ScheduleApi: the level in force, the next level and the unpaused time until it)

ScheduleApi.levelInfo.returns: LevelInfo (the values of a level by number, for example the blinds a hand is dealt at)

levelsFromRules.returns: Level[] (section.levels as levels: label 'Level n', values from the listed fields; default section blinds, default fields small_blind->sb and big_blind->bb)

scheduleFromRules.returns: Schedule (levels as levelsFromRules, levelSeconds from level_duration_seconds, doubling from after_last_level.<field>_multiplier_each_level, all fields agreeing; explicit settings win)

nextLevel.returns: LevelInfo|null (null when a stop schedule has run out)

notes: Engine form: createScheduleApi(schedule) gives levelAt(elapsedMs) and describe(elapsedMs) for a tournament, plus levelInfo(level) for a game that deals at a level. scheduleFromRules builds the schedule from the house rules file (any parsed rules: rules-settings' value layer is not needed). The elapsed argument is the level clock of game-clock (elapsed(clock,'level')).
